faqs.question: What is a good Ganesh Chaturthi quote in Hindi for elders?
faqs.answer: Use the आप form or a Sanskrit shloka. "आपके जीवन से हर विघ्न दूर हो और घर में सुख-समृद्धि का वास हो। गणेश चतुर्थी की हार्दिक शुभकामनाएँ।" is the safest, because आपके marks respect and शुभकामनाएँ is the formal closing. वक्रतुण्ड महाकाय works too and carries no pronoun at all.

faqs.question: Should I send Ganesh Chaturthi wishes in Devanagari or in Roman letters?
faqs.answer: Devanagari if the person reads it comfortably, Roman if they do not. A 2013 fMRI study in Brain and Language found readers had more difficulty identifying words in Romanised Hindi than in either Devanagari or English, so Devanagari is genuinely easier for a Hindi reader.

faqs.question: What does "Ganpati Bappa Morya, agle baras tu jaldi aa" mean?
faqs.answer: It means "Hail Ganpati Bappa — come early next year." It is the chant of visarjan day, which in 2026 is Friday 25 September. Sending it on 14 September is the most common mistake, because it says goodbye before the festival has started.

faqs.question: Is it disrespectful to use तू for Ganesh ji?
faqs.answer: No. With a deity, तू signals intimacy rather than rank, which is why अगले बरस तू जल्दी आ is sung by crowds without anyone objecting. The same तू addressed to a human elder would be an insult.

faqs.question: When is Ganesh Chaturthi in 2026?
faqs.answer: Monday 14 September 2026. The Madhyahna Ganesha puja muhurat for Delhi runs 11:02 AM to 1:31 PM, per Drik Panchang, and the timing shifts by city — Pune is 11:16 AM to 1:44 PM.

faqs.question: What is the shortest Ganesh Chaturthi quote in Hindi for a WhatsApp status?
faqs.answer: "पहला निमंत्रण गणपति को, फिर बाकी सबको" is nine words and fits one line at WhatsApp's default status size. "जिस घर में बप्पा का वास हो, वहाँ दुःख कभी नहीं ठहरता" is slightly longer and still fits without wrapping on most phones.

faqs.question: Can I just translate an English Ganesh Chaturthi wish into Hindi?
faqs.answer: It usually reads wrong. The TyDiP study across nine languages including Hindi found politeness classification degraded when text was machine-translated into English, which suggests politeness marking does not survive translation. Write the Hindi first, then transliterate it if you need Roman letters.

faqs.question: What does "Vakratunda Mahakaya" actually mean?
faqs.answer: "Curved-trunked, mighty one, radiant as ten million suns — make all my undertakings free of obstacles, always." It is the standard invocation before beginning anything new, which is why it is used far beyond Ganesh Chaturthi itself.

faqs.question: Why do Hindi quotes sometimes look broken on my phone?
faqs.answer: Older system fonts drop or mis-stack Devanagari conjuncts such as क्ष and त्र, so a line that looked right on your screen can arrive mangled. Sending the text as real text rather than a screenshot at least lets the recipient's device re-render it correctly.

faqs.question: Is "Ganesh Chaturthi mubarak" correct Hindi?
faqs.answer: It is grammatical and widely understood — मुबारक is Perso-Arabic in origin and completely normal in spoken Hindustani. For a Hindu religious festival many people still prefer शुभकामनाएँ or बधाई, so use मुबारक with friends rather than with an elder you do not know well.

faqs.question: What should I write to a boss or a client on Ganesh Chaturthi?
faqs.answer: Send the shloka. वक्रतुण्ड महाकाय has no second-person pronoun, so it cannot be read as over-familiar, and it is about removing obstacles from work — which is exactly the register a professional message wants.

faqs.question: When is Ganpati visarjan in 2026?
faqs.answer: Friday 25 September 2026, on Anant Chaturdashi, eleven days after Ganesh Chaturthi on Monday 14 September. That is the day अगले बरस तू जल्दी आ belongs on, not the first day.

article.contentMarkdown:
# Ganesh Chaturthi Quotes in Hindi: What to Send, and to Whom

Ganesh Chaturthi 2026 falls on **Monday 14 September**, with the Madhyahna puja muhurat running [11:02 AM to 1:31 PM in Delhi](https://www.drikpanchang.com/festivals/ganesh-chaturthi/ganesh-chaturthi-date-time.html?geoname-id=1273294&year=2026) and visarjan on Friday 25 September. The Hindi quote you send that morning has to match the person: a Sanskrit shloka for an elder, plain Devanagari for a cousin, a Hinglish line for a status. Get the register wrong and it reads as a forward. Below are six Ganesh Chaturthi quotes in Hindi, each in Devanagari with Roman transliteration and an English gloss, plus a rule for choosing between आप and तुम. For scale: across all 3,860 pages SubhSandesh has created since March 2026 — platform-wide, across 15 page types — 49.6% of the 45,656 recorded views are opened on a phone, and 96.1% of started pages are actually published and shared.

## The three registers of Hindi you can text

A "Hindi quote" for Ganesh Chaturthi is one of three different things, and they are not interchangeable.

A **Sanskrit shloka in Devanagari** (वक्रतुण्ड महाकाय) is scripture. It carries no personal pronoun, so it is safe for a manager, a client or a grandmother alike.

**Everyday Hindi in Devanagari** (जिस घर में बप्पा का वास हो) is your own voice, and its politeness is fixed entirely by the pronoun you choose.

**Romanagari** — Hindi typed in Roman letters, usually salted with English — is the register of chat; a 2024 analysis of 262,578 Hindi–English tweets posted between 2014 and 2022 found this blend still spreading. Sending an elder a Romanagari line is not rude, but it is casual in a way a shloka is not. Sending a college friend a full shloka reads as a mass forward.

## Six Ganesh Chaturthi quotes in Hindi, with transliteration and meaning

Each entry gives the Devanagari, a practical Roman transliteration, the English sense, and who it fits.

### 1. वक्रतुण्ड महाकाय — the universal shloka

वक्रतुण्ड महाकाय सूर्यकोटि समप्रभ। निर्विघ्नं कुरु मे देव सर्वकार्येषु सर्वदा॥

*Vakratunda mahakaya suryakoti samaprabha, nirvighnam kuru me deva sarvakaryeshu sarvada.*

"Curved-trunked, mighty one, radiant as ten million suns — make all my undertakings free of obstacles, always."

Who it fits: anyone. It is the standard invocation before starting something new, so it works for a work group and a grandparent equally. No second person, no risk.

### 2. गणपति बप्पा मोरया, अगले बरस तू जल्दी आ

*Ganpati Bappa Morya, agle baras tu jaldi aa.*

"Hail Ganpati Bappa — come early next year."

The visarjan chant, shouted in the street rather than written. Note the तू: addressed to a deity it is intimacy, not disrespect. Save it for 25 September; sent on the 14th it wishes Bappa away before he arrives.

### 3. जिस घर में बप्पा का वास हो, वहाँ दुःख कभी नहीं ठहरता

*Jis ghar mein Bappa ka vaas ho, wahan dukh kabhi nahin thaharta.*

"Where Bappa lives, sorrow never stays."

No second-person pronoun at all, which makes it the safest personal line here — it goes to an uncle and a flatmate unchanged, and it fits a status without wrapping.

### 4. आपके जीवन से हर विघ्न दूर हो — the formal wish

आपके जीवन से हर विघ्न दूर हो और घर में सुख-समृद्धि का वास हो। गणेश चतुर्थी की हार्दिक शुभकामनाएँ।

*Aapke jeevan se har vighn door ho aur ghar mein sukh-samriddhi ka vaas ho. Ganesh Chaturthi ki hardik shubhkamnayein.*

"May every obstacle leave your life and may happiness and prosperity live in your home. Warm wishes on Ganesh Chaturthi."

आपके marks respect. This is the line for in-laws, teachers, clients, and anyone whose name you would not use on its own.

### 5. मोदक जैसा मीठा दिन हो, बप्पा जैसा बड़ा दिल

*Modak jaisa meetha din ho, Bappa jaisa bada dil.*

"May your day be as sweet as a modak and your heart as big as Bappa's."

Warm and a little silly, which is why it works between friends and siblings. Add दोस्त or their name and leave शुभकामनाएँ off — the formal closing fights the joke.

### 6. पहला निमंत्रण गणपति को, फिर बाकी सबको

*Pehla nimantran Ganpati ko, phir baaki sabko.*

"The first invitation goes to Ganpati; everyone else after."

A nod to Ganesha as प्रथम पूज्य, the first worshipped in any rite. Nine words, so it survives an Instagram caption crop, and specific enough not to read like a template.

## आप, तुम or तू: the pronoun decides how it lands

Hindi forces a politeness choice English does not. आप is respect and distance, तुम is peer-level warmth, and तू is either intimacy or an insult depending entirely on who says it to whom. The wrong pronoun is not a grammar mistake but a social one, and the recipient notices it before reading the wish.

The working rule: आप for anyone older, anyone senior at work, and anyone you address by a title. तुम for cousins, friends and siblings. तू only where you already use it in speech — and with Bappa, where the tradition licenses it.

This is also why running an English line through a translator is a bad way to produce these. [TyDiP, a nine-language politeness dataset that includes Hindi](https://aclanthology.org/2022.findings-emnlp.420/) (EMNLP 2022, 500 annotated examples per language) reports that classification accuracy drops when target-language text is machine-translated into English first — the authors read that as politeness not surviving translation. Write the Hindi, then transliterate it.

If the line is doing more work than a text can carry, [a Ganesh Chaturthi page the recipient performs themselves](https://subhsandesh.in/happy-ganesh-chaturthi) puts your words at the end of a ritual they complete: they offer the durva, kumkum, flowers and modak, the aarti thali circles while Karpur Gauram plays, and they write their own prarthana back to you.

## What Roman letters actually do to a Hindi line

Romanagari is not a neutral container for Hindi. An fMRI study of Hindi–English bilinguals, ['Cost in transliteration' in Brain and Language](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.bandl.2012.12.004) (2013), found readers had greater difficulty identifying concrete words in Romanised Hindi than in either Devanagari or English, the extra effort showing as heavier recruitment of language and attention networks. The full text is paywalled; that finding is from the published abstract.

The cause is that Roman Hindi has no agreed spelling. A 2025 EMNLP paper on [informally romanised language identification](https://aclanthology.org/2025.emnlp-main.117/) notes that romanisation makes languages which are trivially separable in their own scripts — Hindi and Urdu — highly confusable, and its best system reaches 88.2% F1 identifying the language of romanised text across 20 Indic languages. If a purpose-built classifier misses roughly one line in eight, your keyboard's autocorrect will do worse.

None of that makes Devanagari the automatic answer. Code-mixing is now the default register: a study of 262,578 tweets from 16,710 handles posted between 2014 and 2022 found [Hinglish adoption growing at an annualised 1.2%](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41599-024-03058-6), with Hinglish usage on the platform rising about 2% a year and the median code-mixing index reaching 0.57 in its 2020–2022 window. Send a 22-year-old cousin a pure Sanskrit shloka and you have mismatched the register in the other direction.

## Four ways to send it, compared

The choice is not only who can read the script — it is what breaks in transit.

| Way to send it | Who can read it | What breaks | SubhSandesh data (platform-wide, all 15 page types) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Devanagari text in a chat | Devanagari readers only | Old system fonts drop conjuncts like क्ष and त्र; the sender needs a Hindi keyboard | Not measured — plain chat never touches the platform |
| Roman transliteration | Everyone who reads English letters | No standard spelling; romanised Indic language ID tops out at 88.2% F1 | Not measured |
| A screenshot or forwarded image | Devanagari readers only | Text is not selectable, searchable or screen-readable | Not measured |
| A shared page carrying both scripts | Everyone | Needs a data connection at the moment of opening | 49.6% of 45,656 views arrive on a phone; 96.1% of 3,860 started pages get published |

Only the last two rows survive a recipient who cannot read Devanagari, and only the last keeps the Hindi as real, selectable text.

## Writing a status that does not read like a forward

A Ganesh Chaturthi status is read in under two seconds, so length matters more than eloquence. Quotes 3, 5 and 6 above are all under twelve words in Devanagari and fit a single line at WhatsApp's default status type size.

Two habits separate a written status from a forwarded one: name something local — your mandap, your building's visarjan procession, the 40 modaks your mother made — and pick one script and stay in it. A line that starts in Devanagari and finishes in Roman looks like a copy-paste seam, because usually it is one.

If you are posting on 25 September rather than 14 September, change the verb. अगले बरस तू जल्दी आ is a farewell; using it on day one is the single most common Ganesh Chaturthi status error, and Hindi readers catch it instantly.

## When a Hindi quote — or a SubhSandesh page — is the wrong thing to send

A quote is the wrong medium when you are in the same city. Standing at the mandap with someone beats any line you could type, and no page can hand anyone a modak. For a grandparent who does not open links, a phone call in Hindi beats a well-transliterated message and takes less time.

The platform data argues against itself here too. 42.1% of SubhSandesh creators password-protect a page before sharing it (1,625 of 3,860, platform-wide) — sensible for a love letter, actively wrong for a festival greeting that should be forwardable to a family group. And 49.6% of views arriving on a phone means 50.4% do not, so if your recipient reads everything on a desktop at work, a plain Devanagari message is the lower-friction choice.

SubhSandesh is also wrong if you want a printed card, a rangoli stencil or a prasad delivery. It makes one thing: a link. If you do want that link, the [full template gallery](https://subhsandesh.in/templates) covers the other 14 page types.

- [Improving Informally Romanized Language Identification](https://aclanthology.org/2025.emnlp-main.117/), *Proceedings of EMNLP 2025*.

auditReport.honestAssessment: Every page ranking for this keyword is a Devanagari quote dump — FNP's page contains zero Devanagari characters at all, and none of the five gives a Roman transliteration, an English gloss, or any guidance on which pronoun fits which recipient. This post is the only one that pairs all three per quote and grounds the script decision in Rao et al. (2013), the 2025 EMNLP romanised-LID result and the 2024 Hinglish code-mixing study, plus first-party numbers no competitor can print. Against that: the first-party data is platform-wide across 15 page types with zero Ganesh pages created, so it is context rather than segment evidence; subhsandesh.in has far less domain authority than the quote farms and Adobe Express, and this is a seasonal query with a two-week window. Expect citation by answer engines before ranking movement, if either happens.
